Chapter 10: After the Applause—Business, Ownership, and the Search for Purpose
You know, retirement can feel like stepping into the unknown—especially for athletes. All those routines that shaped everyday life? Suddenly, they’re gone. And that big question—what comes next?—starts to echo. For Michael, this next chapter was a mix of challenge and excitement. That competitive spark? It didn’t just disappear. It just needed a new place to shine.
Business became his new playing field. Everything he’d learned on the court—discipline, preparation, being willing to take risks—all of it fit perfectly in the world of entrepreneurship. Michael started investing in teams, launching new brands, and building partnerships that stretched his influence way beyond basketball. The same drive that pushed him as a player now fueled his ventures off the court.
But let’s talk about ownership—because that’s a whole different game. Running a team isn’t the same as leading one on the floor. The stakes are higher, decisions get more complicated, and there’s always someone watching, analyzing every move. There were incredible highs—those moments when a bold idea paid off, or when a vision finally became reality. But there were setbacks, too. Deals didn’t always go through. Some seasons just ended with disappointment. And, as always, the most valuable lessons were learned the hard way.
And then there’s the search for purpose. Turns out, fame alone doesn’t fill that need. Michael started feeling a bigger pull—to use his platform for something more. Giving back, mentoring, advocating for issues he cared about—these things became a huge part of his life. He poured energy into causes close to his heart, helped open doors for others, and spoke out when it mattered most.
Of course, the path wasn’t always smooth. The pressures of business, the weight of leadership, the constant spotlight—they all took their toll. But those old lessons—resilience, adaptability, never stopping the learning process—stayed just as important as ever.
Most people? They see the headlines, the deals, the public appearances. But what they don’t see are the quiet moments—the late-night reflection, the struggle to find balance, that ever-present search for meaning. When the applause fades, that’s when the real work begins. The work of building a life that truly matters.
